title: Enterprise Onboarding, Escalation & QBR Playbook
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Overview:
This document consolidates the end-to-end enterprise onboarding playbook, escalation procedures, integration checklist, common known issues and workarounds, and the structure for health checks and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) for Redwood Inference customers. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Support Engineers, Solutions Engineers, and relevant product and SRE stakeholders.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Provide a repeatable, high-quality onboarding experience that reduces time-to-value, minimizes incident risk during ramp, and establishes a measurable QBR cadence.
- Scope: Applies to all paid enterprise customers deploying Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private (VPC/on-prem) offerings.

High-level onboarding phases (summary):
1) Pre-sales handoff
   - Deliverables: signed contract, technical intake questionnaire, SSO/KMS requirements, expected throughput and latency targets, compliance needs.
   - Owner: CSM (primary), Solutions Engineering (technical validation).
2) Kickoff (Week 0)
   - Agenda: introductions, roles/responsibilities, success criteria, initial timeline, security review.
   - Deliverables: Kickoff notes, access lists, IP allowlist if needed.
3) Integration & configuration (Weeks 1-4)
   - Tasks: network connectivity, auth (API keys, SSO/OIDC), model routing config, quota/SLA configuration, observability hooks (tracing, logs).
   - Owners: Solutions Engineering & Customer Engineering.
4) Validation & load testing (Weeks 3-6)
   - Tasks: perf runbook, baseline metrics (p50/p95 latency, throughput), safety/regression tests (sample prompts), quality guardrail checks.
   - Owners: CS, SE, Eng SRE.
5) Go-Live and hypercare (Go-Live + 2-4 weeks)
   - Activities: increased monitoring, daily syncs (first week), immediate escalation paths, knowledge transfer.
6) Transition to standard support & QBR cadence
   - After hypercare: move to standard monthly health checks and quarterly business reviews.

Detailed onboarding checklist (operational tasks):
- Pre-kickoff: obtain contract, security & network questionnaire answers, list of integration owners, data residency requirements.
- Access: create RBAC roles, provision API keys, configure SSO (SAML/OIDC) and KMS integration if requested.
- Networking: provide IP ranges and DNS endpoints; validate egress/inbound rules; VPN or private link instructions for Private deployments.
- Model mapping: confirm model families, latencies required, token accounting expectations, and fallback model choices.
- Observability: instrument routes with tracing; enable per-route token cost analytics; grant read-only console access to customer's monitoring account where applicable.
- Security & compliance: if restricted, collect required SOC2/ISO artifacts; sign DPA; run penetration test schedule.

Roles & responsibilities (RACI-style):
- Customer Success Manager (CSM): overall owner of the onboarding timeline and business success criteria.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): technical integration lead and runbook author.
- Customer Engineering / Onsite Engineer (if Dedicated/Private): implements network and on-prem packaging.
- Support Engineer (Tier 2/3): incident response & escalations.
- Product/SRE: policy, bug fixes, platform capacity adjustments.

Escalation playbook (operational):
- Severity definitions and target response times:
  - Sev1 (Critical production outage): Total outage or >50% feature failure impacting customers. Target acknowledgement: 15 minutes; Target mitigation timeline: 2 hours for workaround.
  - Sev2 (Partial outage / severe degradation): Significant impairment (e.g., high p95 latency, >5% error rate). Acknowledgement: 30 minutes; Mitigation: 4-24 hours.
  - Sev3 (Minor issue / non-critical): Feature impact limited or workaround exists. Acknowledgement: 4 business hours; Mitigation: next release or patch.

- Escalation path:
1) Tier 1 (Support): initial triage, collect logs, confirm scope, attempt documented workarounds.
2) Tier 2 (Support Engineer / SE on-call): deeper debugging, reproduce locally, validate recent deploys or configuration changes.
3) Tier 3 (SRE / Runtime Team / Product): fixes for infra/runtime issues, patch or rollback decisions.
4) Executive escalation: triggered for major incidents (Sev1 > 6 hours or customer P0 business impact). Notify CSM, VP CS, VP Eng; coordinate public comms.

- Information to collect (initial triage):
  - Customer name, region, deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
  - Route/model IDs, timestamps, request IDs, p95 latency and error rate trends
  - Recent changes: configuration, model rollouts, infra capacity changes
  - Relevant logs: API gateway, runtime logs, kernel scheduler traces, GPU utilization charts

- Playbook actions (examples):
  - High latency on Hosted API: check model variant fallback, autoscaling status, queue depth, KV cache hit rates; temporarily route traffic to lower-latency model if configured.
  - Token billing spike: validate prompt sizes, rate limit misconfiguration, examine batch sizing; freeze new model rollouts and open an account-level audit.

Integration guide (concise checklist and examples):
- Auth and secrets:
  - Preferred: API keys for server-to-server, SSO (OIDC/SAML) for user-facing console access.
  - Example: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate
- Network connectivity:
  - Hosted: ensure outbound HTTPS to our API endpoints; optional IP allowlist if customer firewall is strict.
  - Dedicated/Private: follow provided VPC/peering instructions; for on-prem, verify hostnames in /etc/hosts or DNS entries.
- Rate limits and quotas:
  - Document expected rate limits per account and per-model route. Configure retry/backoff per SDK guidance.
- Observability hooks:
  - Recommend enabling request-level traces and attaching synthetic prompt tests. Provide example tracing headers and sample log format.

Known issues and workarounds (living list):
- ISSUE-2025-014: Occasional p95 spikes for long sequences on quantized models
  - Symptoms: p95 latency increases with sequence lengths > 1024 tokens.
  - Workaround: route long-sequence requests to full-precision variant or increase batch_timeout to favor throughput.
  - Owner: Runtime team; fix planned in kernel scheduler 2026-03 release.
- ISSUE-2025-027: Intermittent 401 during SSO session refresh for some IdPs
  - Symptoms: users experience brief login failures when SSO token refresh occurs.
  - Workaround: instruct customers to increase session lifetime or use API key for service accounts.
  - Owner: Identity & Security.
- ISSUE-2025-048: Dedicate cluster autoscaler overreacts under burst traffic
  - Symptoms: unnecessary scale-ups resulting in transient cold starts.
  - Workaround: apply temporary scaling policy cap and enable warm-pool feature.
  - Owner: Infra / Capacity planning.

Health checks & QBR materials (metrics and cadence):
- Monthly health checks (CSM cadence):
  - Metrics to review: total tokens/month, avg cost/token, p50/p95 latency, error rate (4xx/5xx), cache hit ratio, model quality regressions (based on eval prompt sets).
  - Operational items: open incidents, change requests, upcoming model rollouts.
  - Deliverable: 1-page status summary and action item list.
- Quarterly Business Reviews (QBR) template:
  - Agenda: business outcomes, adoption & usage trends, reliability & incidents review, cost optimization opportunities, roadmap & feature asks, open action items.
  - Slides: 8-12 slides including metrics, top 3 recommendations, next quarter objectives.
  - Owners: CSM (lead), SE (technical sections), Customer (present use cases).

QBR recommended KPIs (examples):
- Adoption: active routes, requests/week, new features adopted
- Performance: p50/p95 latency, success rate, SLO attainment (monthly objective: 99.9% request success, p95 latency < target per-contract)
- Cost & efficiency: tokens per successful transaction, recommended quantization/ batching savings realized
- Quality: sample prompt pass rate (guardrail tests), percentage of model regressions detected and remediated

Templates and artifacts (links and examples):
- Kickoff agenda template: /confluence/templates/kickoff-agenda
- Integration runbook template: /confluence/templates/integration-runbook
- QBR slide deck template: /confluence/templates/qbr-template
- Incident postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template

Knowledge transfer and documentation handoff:
- Deliver the integration runbook and run a 90-minute handoff workshop with the customer's platform team.
- Provide read-only console access for 30 days post-go-live and archive the runbook in the customer folder.

- Review cadence: Annual full review, with ad-hoc updates after Sev1 incidents or major product changes.
- Where to propose changes: open PR against this page and add reviewers: Product, SRE, Solutions Engineering.
